args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP despite its docstring
promising banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212. This made
tests/test_money.py::test_half_even fail in the nightly build, since
2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of the Banker's-rounded 2.66.

Switch the import and quantize call to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.body:
## Summary
Fixes the nightly build failure in tests/test_money.py.

`round_money` in src/money.py was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP even though its docstring promised banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212. As a result, `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` returned `2.67` instead of the banker's-rounded `2.66`, failing test_half_even in the nightly build.

## Changes
- Import ROUND_HALF_EVEN instead of ROUND_HALF_UP in src/money.py.
- Quantize with rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

## Verification
CI run ci-0001 (sha 08d3cd5986) passed on branch fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding.

transcript.reasoning_content:
Interesting — test expects 2.675 → 2.68 and 2.665 → 2.66. Note 2.665 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN gives 2.66 (even), and ROUND_HALF_UP gives 2.67. So test fails with current code for 2.665. But 2.675 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN... 2.675 → the digit to round, 7 is followed by 5 only, so it's exactly half → round to even → 2.68 (since 7→8? Let's think: 2.675 quantize to 2 decimals: last kept digit is 7, remainder .5 exactly → round half to even → 2.68 because 8 is even). Yes, 2.68. Good.

So fix: change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Create branch, commit, run CI, open PR, merge (merge requires approval from code-owner — policy says merging into main requires approval; merge_pr may be routed to approver). Let's proceed.
